\lcCategory{With the paper's hypotheses; Lean proves a narrower conclusion.}{7}
\begin{lcTable}
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}{4.1.2} & Auxiliary mask norm\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves, under \lcRef{Hypothesis}{H:homog}{1.2.1} and $\Gamma\neq0$, that $\nu_R$ is even, tempered and Radon, the ball bound \lcRef{Equation}{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}{4.1.5} uniformly in $R>0$, and \lcRef{Equation}{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}{4.1.6} for a separable complex Hilbert space $H$ (indeed any complex Banach space) with integrability and a finite right side; the clause for a real $H$ after complexification is not formalized.} \\
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:variational-global-mean}{7.3.2} & Global regularity of the original mean\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves the display \lcRef{Equation}{E:variational-global-mean}{7.3.3} on $I=[0,1]$ ($0\le h_s\le M$ and $\|h_s-h_t\|_\infty\le C_\Psi|s-t|$, with integrability, continuity in $x$ and a joint Lipschitz bound); the first sentence, that every mixed time and space derivative of $h_s$ is globally bounded, is not formalized.} \\
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-unmasked-rate}{7.3.3} & The unmasked Rayleigh rate\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves the Rayleigh-form part with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied: for $\lambda$ defined by the real Rayleigh supremum \lcRef{Equation}{E:variational-real-rayleigh}{7.3.4}, a uniform positive floor, the Lipschitz bounds and $I_\Psi$ positive and finite; the operator statements ($H_s$ self-adjoint, form domain $H^1$, spectral bottom $E_s$, $\lambda=\sqrt{-E_s}$) are not formalized.} \\
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:variational-control-dilation}{7.3.5} & Radon and Rayleigh dilation\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves the bijection and the four identities with the section's hypotheses (\lcRef{Hypothesis}{H:homog}{1.2.1}, $\Gamma\neq0$, $a=\alpha_0$) and nothing supplied, for the variance in its integral form and the rate defined by the real Rayleigh supremum \lcRef{Equation}{E:variational-real-rayleigh}{7.3.4}; their identification with $\E W(\Psi)^2$ (\lcRef{Lemma}{L:compact-raw-profile}{6.3.6}) and $\sqrt{-E_s}$ (\lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-unmasked-rate}{7.3.3}) is not formalized.} \\
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:spatial-static-controls}{8.2.2} & Smooth temporal controls\newline{\footnotesize $\lambda$ is the supremum of the real Rayleigh quotient and $I_\Psi$, $v_\Psi$ are given by their integral formulas (identification with $\sqrt{-E_s}$ and $\E W(\Psi)^2$ is not formalized); \lcRef{Equation}{E:spatial-static-score}{8.2.2} is proved in the form that every number below the bound is exceeded by some admissible score, and its form as a supremum rests on a named input, the boundedness claim of \lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-positive-scores}{7.3.6}.} \\
  \lcRef{Proposition}{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}{8.2.3} & The finite smooth spatial ratio\newline{\footnotesize \lcRef{Equation}{E:spatial-smooth-score}{8.2.3} is proved in the form that every $y$ below the bound is exceeded by some $I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2$ ($\lambda$ the supremum of the real Rayleigh quotient, $v_\Psi$ given by its integral formula); its form as a supremum rests on a named input, the boundedness claim of \lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-positive-scores}{7.3.6}. $R_0<\infty$ is proved without that input, by a direct Fourier bound.} \\
  \lcRef{Lemma}{L:tube-rayleigh-tail}{10.2.7} & Exact Rayleigh tail bound\newline{\footnotesize Lean proves the bound with integrability and the finite head integral; the ``In particular'' application to the coarse-envelope bound of another proposition is not formalized.} \\
\end{lcTable}
